Maya - thanks for the clear list. Answers inline below and attached a SOC2 summary + integration guide for your GRC review.

1) Isolation: Redwood supports per-tenant key scoping and isolated projects/environments. In Dedicated/Private deployments you can additionally enforce network segmentation (VPC). For hosted accounts, each tenant has isolated API keys/service accounts and separate audit streams.

2) Rotation: recommended patterns:
   - Service accounts -> short-lived JWTs (recommended) using your IdP or our token exchange.
   - If you need long-lived credentials, use KMS-wrapped keys and rotate the underlying material every 30 days.
   - Redwood supports automatic rotation hooks and can be configured to rotate keys against a linked KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) - we store only encrypted key material when required.

3) Audit logs: attached "soc2-summary.pdf" includes sample audit log extracts (token issuance, rotation events, admin-api calls). Logs are exportable to your SIEM via a push or S3 sink.

4) Least privilege / scoping: yes - tokens can be scoped by role to restrict to embeddings-only, generation-only, or particular model variants. We also support route-level policies in the Console so you can limit access by route or endpoint.

Attachments: soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-integration-guide.pdf

Proposed engineering sync agenda (30m):
- 5m: quick intros and goals
- 10m: auth flows (service accounts, JWTs, token exchange) + SDK demo
- 10m: audit logs, rotation, KMS options
- 5m: next steps and handoffs

I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 11/03 10:00am PT. If that doesn't work, alternate slots Thu 11/04 9:00am or Fri 11/05 11:00am PT.
